candidate_findings.title: Claimed wave limit dimensions have no numeric defaults or hard ceilings
candidate_findings.gap: The canonical default list supplies children, waves, microusd, estimated tokens, wall-clock time, retries, and backoff, while acceptance additionally requires bytes, refs, write targets, and tool rounds to be measurable and to block on hard-limit exceedance. No values, units, or aggregation rules for those additional dimensions are provided.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Admission cannot decide whether a wave exceeds a hard limit in the omitted dimensions, making the block-on-exceedance obligation unverifiable and allowing supposedly bounded inputs or tool use to expand without a deterministic ceiling.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify numeric defaults and hard maxima, units, counting/aggregation rules, zero/unlimited semantics, override authority, and exact blocked_reason_code behavior for every claimed dimension.

candidate_findings.title: Parallel waves lack atomic budget reservation and usage reconciliation
candidate_findings.gap: OSI-428 requires cost-aware parallelism, cost-ceiling receipts, and limits below the parent remaining budget, but defines no reservation, commit, release, refund, or actual-versus-estimated usage transition shared by concurrently admitted children or waves.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two concurrent admissions can each observe the same remaining budget and both pass, oversubscribing the parent envelope. Late provider charges, cancellations, and retries can then make recorded ceilings disagree with actual spend.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define an atomic per-run budget ledger with pending, reserved, charged, released, and exhausted states; compare-and-swap admission; estimation rules; actual-usage reconciliation; overrun handling; and receipt/event ordering.

candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A timed-out child and its retry can both commit; two differently named paths can overlap the same live surface; a cancelled parent can accept late output; and partial mandatory-child failure can leave unverifiable mutations.

candidate_findings.title: Certification authority relies on undefined low-end and high-end classifications
candidate_findings.gap: The plan says roles remain distinct, records certification_tier only when applicable, forbids low-end completion certification, and requires high-end certification, but it never defines the authoritative mapping from runtime identity/capability/model to role or tier, separation of duties, self-certification rules, quorum, or behavior when an eligible certifier is unavailable.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A child can be mislabeled as high-end, an executor can certify its own work, or a parent can choose a weaker certifier without a machine-checkable policy, defeating completion and governance-unlock boundaries.
